doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Technology versus pencil and manuscript
summary: He works more on computer now, does not miss drudgery, and joke about his illegible handwriting.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh yes. Your career has gone from splicing tape and using a pencil and pad to today where things seem to change almost every year. Are there positives and negatives for you?

Yeah I think so. I mean I still try to put, if I’m composing, ideas down on paper and then transfer them to the computer. When I’m arranging lately I’ve done a lot more, although I’m sort of sketching stuff out, a lot more of the basic work I’ve been doing on the computer rather than on manuscript. But I’d like to say I miss that old way of doing it,

but I don’t think I really miss it. I don’t think that’s the right sentence. All that drudgery. Plus the fact that I wound up in the position where I couldn’t read my own writing so I don’t know how anyone else did. It’s got worse and worst. My copyist used to say, “I can read your musical stuff but it’s the directions that I haven’t a clue what you’ve written — make a guess at, does that say ‘adagio’ or ‘allegro’ or what does it say?”
Does that say PAL or does that say something else.
Yes. “Have you got a video, pal.” Funny.
